title: Natural comparison of geometric-point inverse-image global sections with the stalk
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field and $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. For a sheaf of sets $F$ on $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], write $G=(\mathrm{id}\circ s)^{-1}F$ for its inverse image [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. There is a natural isomorphism in $F$, $c_F:\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,G)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_s$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For every etale neighbourhood $W\to S$, lift $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$ of $s$, morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ whose first projection is $t$, and $\sigma\in F(W)$, the comparison satisfies $c_F(G(a)(\eta_F(\sigma)))=\operatorname{germ}_{W,t}(\sigma)$, where $\eta_F$ is the inverse-image unit and germs are the colimit coprojections of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

proof.text: For each F, choose the bijective inverse-image stalk comparison d_F for s and the identity point using [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ]. The identity-neighbourhood global-section germ g_F is bijective by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant]. Thus d_F composed with g_F is bijective.

proof.text: Every original stalk element is a germ of a section by the set-colimit description [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Given z in the inverse-image stalk, represent d_F(z) by such a germ. The germ formula for d_F and its injectivity show z is the unit-pulled germ of that representative.

proof.text: For a sheaf morphism psi, evaluate both composites d with the stalk maps on those unit-pulled germs. Naturality of the inverse-image unit, clause (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and naturality of stalk coprojections give equality. Naturality of g_F then makes the bijections d_F composed with g_F into a natural isomorphism.

proof.text: The fibre map of a carries the identity point to the canonical pullback lift: equality of first projections is the hypothesis, and equality of second projections is the over condition. The pullback universal property proves equality of lifts. The stalk restriction relation identifies the global-section germ of G(a)(eta_F(sigma)) with the pointed pulled germ. Apply the germ formula of d_F.

theorem etaleGeometricPointSectionsStalkNatural
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) :
    ∃ c : Scheme.etaleSetPullback (𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω)) ≫ s) ⋙
        (sheafSections (Spec (.of Ω)).smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))).obj
          (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω))))) ≅
        (Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber,
      ∀ (F : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) (W : S.Etale)
        (t : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).fiber.obj W)
        (a : Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω))) ⟶
          (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ (𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω)) ≫ s)).obj W)
        (σ : F.obj.obj (op W)),
        a.left ≫ CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback.fst W.hom (𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω)) ≫ s) =
          t.left →
        (c.hom.app F) (((Scheme.etaleSetPullback (𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω)) ≫ s)).obj F).obj.map a.op
            (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
              (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ (𝟙 (Spec (.of Ω)) ≫ s))
              (Type (u + 1)) (S.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
              ((Spec (.of Ω)).smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app F).hom.app
                (op W) σ)) =
          (Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).toPresheafFiber W t F.obj σ
